user.job: Decide whether LangGraph checkpoint capability is worth a bounded adapter probe while ZAgenticLoop keeps native execution, Evidence, Human acceptance, security, and lifecycle authority.

baseline.workflow: The current ZAgenticLoop working-tree snapshot defines a native checkpoint fixture and resume oracle around work-item identity, checkpoint metadata, state digest, duplicate delivery, Evidence, verification, Human acceptance, and native-core authority.
failureModes: An external checkpoint layer may create a second execution authority or change native execution identity during resume.
A storage contract may be mistaken for complete interrupt/resume semantics or for a Node.js integration seam.
State, Evidence, verification, or Human acceptance may drift from the resumed native work item.
A Python-oriented dependency may expand runtime, version-skew, security, and removal obligations beyond a narrow adapter.

targetOutcome: A reviewable decision and conformance plan for an isolated LangGraph checkpoint/resume capability probe, with explicit unknowns and a removal path back to the native fixture.
goals: Verify whether LangGraph's checkpoint storage contract can map to the native checkpoint fixture.
Preserve native execution identity, duplicate semantics, Evidence binding, verification, Human acceptance, and lifecycle ownership.
Separate a durable-state adapter from whole-framework adoption.
Make the missing resume, Node.js, security, and version-boundary evidence explicit.
Define measurable continue, defer, or stop gates for the probe.
nonGoals: Adopting LangGraph as the Graph/OPN core.
Implementing a production checkpoint service or Python runtime deployment in this research run.
Letting LangGraph own approvals, credentials, sandboxing, Evidence, verification, Human acceptance, or lifecycle closeout.
Treating the fresh ledger's stars or topicMatch as capability or product-fit scores.

constraints.statement: ZAgenticLoop native core remains the sole authority for execution identity, lifecycle, Evidence, verification, Human acceptance, security policy, and closeout.
The adapter must pass the native fixture's positive and hard-stop cases, including duplicate delivery, digest drift, identity change, and authority bypass.
The host product is TypeScript/Node.js; a Python-oriented checkpointer cannot be treated as a native dependency without an explicit runtime and ownership decision.
Every external capability claim must trace to the A34 v2 sealed ledger; unverified resume and Node/TS behavior remain unknown.
Removing the adapter must leave the native checkpoint fixture and resume oracle passing without rewriting native facts.

assumptions: The A34 code-research snapshot is representative of the active checkpoint probe boundary, even though its working tree is dirty and explicitly fingerprinted.
LangGraph's checkpoint conformance surface is a serious unit-capability candidate, not evidence that the whole framework fits ZAgenticLoop.
A narrow experience-version probe is the right lifecycle stage before any durable runtime commitment.
decisionScope: LangGraph checkpoint/resume as a removable unit capability in ZAgenticLoop, including the native adapter envelope, unknown closure, hard-stop conformance, and removal gate.

options.name: Keep the native checkpoint fixture and defer external integration
Probe LangGraph checkpoint storage behind a provider-neutral adapter
Adopt LangGraph as the Graph/OPN checkpoint authority
